title: Oka coherence and local coherent free resolutions

items.title: Oka coherence and local coherent free resolutions
items.statement: Assume AC. On every finite-dimensional complex manifold M the holomorphic structure sheaf O_M is coherent: the relation sheaf of any finite tuple of local holomorphic sections is locally finitely generated. Coherent O_M-modules are closed under kernels, cokernels and finite extensions. For every coherent F, point x and finite integer l≥0, there is a chart neighborhood W of x on which F has an exact partial free resolution O_W^{p_l}→…→O_W^{p_0}→F|_W→0 by finite ranks. Exactness at the leftmost term is not asserted. No global analytic free resolution is claimed.
items.strategy: Prove the Weierstrass-induction relation lemma with generators uniform on one neighborhood, following Demailly II3.19–3.20. Handle zero/unit tuple entries and coordinate changes. Prove the elementary coherent-kernel calculus and obtain each finite partial resolution by successive coherent kernels and finite shrinking. Stalk Noetherianity alone is insufficient.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC; record resolutions, countable shrinking/diagonal choices, Baire/Fréchet arguments and supplier-inherited choice uses precisely. No physical premise.

title: Faithful flatness of finite-type algebraic-to-analytic local rings

items.title: Faithful flatness of finite-type algebraic-to-analytic local rings
items.statement: Assume AC. Let X be a finite-type complex scheme, x a complex closed point, and define X^an locally by extending a finite polynomial defining ideal to convergent holomorphic functions, retaining nilpotents. The canonical local map A=O_{X,x}→B=O_{X^an,x} is injective and faithfully flat; its induced map on maximal-ideal completions is an isomorphism. In Serre’s flat-pair convention, B/A is flat over A and M→M⊗_A B is injective for every A-module M. On an affine ambient chart at x, C[t]_(t) and C{t} have common completion C[[t]], and the quotient comparison is compatible with every finitely generated defining ideal. This is a local-ring assertion, not a relative direct-image theorem.
items.strategy: Identify finite jets on polynomial local and convergent rings by truncation and finite degree-k monomial grouping of convergent tails. Apply existing completion flatness: T is flat over A and faithfully flat over B. For each injection of A-modules tensor its B-kernel with T, use A-flatness of T and faithful reflection to get zero kernel. Prove local faithfulness and unit injection, then Tor gives B/A flat. Pass to the same extended defining ideal for finite-type quotients; do not invoke reduced-set Nullstellensatz.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC; record resolutions, countable shrinking/diagonal choices, Baire/Fréchet arguments and supplier-inherited choice uses precisely. No physical premise.

title: Local coherent acyclicity on sufficiently small polydiscs

items.title: Local coherent acyclicity on sufficiently small polydiscs
items.statement: Assume AC. Let F be coherent analytic on a neighborhood of a point x in C^N. There is a coordinate polydisc W about x such that for every nonempty coordinate polydisc D⊂W and every q>0, H^q(D,F|_D)=0. Scalar sheaf cohomology on such D is computed by its smooth Dolbeault resolution. One can choose W subordinate to a partial finite-rank free resolution of F of length exceeding 2N. The assertion is local in the supplied resolution neighborhood; no untwisted projective Cartan A/B or global Stein generation theorem is asserted.
items.strategy: Write scalar Dolbeault sheaf exactness from the local lemma and smooth-module acyclicity, then global scalar polydisc vanishing. Establish the ordinary sheaf cohomological-dimension bound H^j(D,G)=0 for j>2N for arbitrary abelian sheaves on a polydisc, by explicit finite-order refinements/paracompact Čech comparison, not by misusing a compact-support bound. Choose a partial free resolution longer than 2N on W; dimension shift along its coherent kernels on every D⊂W. No global Cartan A/B.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC; record resolutions, countable shrinking/diagonal choices, Baire/Fréchet arguments and supplier-inherited choice uses precisely. No physical premise.

title: Finite-dimensional coherent cohomology on compact projective space

items.title: Finite-dimensional coherent cohomology on compact projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. For 0≤r≤3 and any coherent analytic O_{P^r(C)}-module F, every H^q(P^r(C),F), q≥0, is finite-dimensional. With the locally defined coherent-section Fréchet topology and the induced Čech quotient topology these cohomology groups are Hausdorff. The proof includes the required Fréchet open-mapping and Schwartz compact-complex finiteness results, local coherent-section topology, and compactness of restriction; none is presumed to follow from a Banach-only or one-variable theorem.
items.strategy: Develop metrizable complete locally convex section spaces and prove the Fréchet open-mapping theorem by Baire and successive approximation; Banach open mapping is only an analogy. Prove Schwartz compact-perturbation and its compact morphism of Fréchet complexes finite-dimensional/Hausdorff cohomology corollary. Define coherent section topology as a closed-relation quotient and show chart/generator independence using Artin–Rees/Krull. Prove several-variable Montel from polydisc Cauchy estimates, Ascoli and diagonal compact exhaustion (the imported named Montel theorem is plane-only). Prove compact coherent restriction maps. Construct finite nested Leray covers of P^r subordinate to distinguished resolution neighborhoods and justify all finite-intersection acyclicity. If intersections are not coordinate polydiscs, explicitly prove their pseudoconvex chart geometry and scalar Dolbeault vanishing, then coherent dimension shifting; do not apply pair3 to arbitrary intersections. Apply the proved compact-complex theorem to the resulting restriction of Čech complexes. This contains substantial internal prerequisites and remains unproved.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC; record resolutions, countable shrinking/diagonal choices, Baire/Fréchet arguments and supplier-inherited choice uses precisely. No physical premise.

title: Projective Dolbeault comparison and scalar structure-sheaf cohomology

items.title: Projective Dolbeault comparison and scalar structure-sheaf cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC. For 0≤r≤3, any holomorphic vector bundle E on P^r(C) has its analytic sheaf cohomology naturally identified with the cohomology of the global smooth E-valued Dolbeault complex. In particular H^0(P^r,O)=C and H^q(P^r,O)=0 for q>0. The scalar vanishing is proved by a direct Laurent/Čech calculation on the standard affine cover, including its acyclic intersections and convergent cochain contractions. This statement does not assume GAGA, higher-dimensional Kähler Hodge theory, or arbitrary-coherent projective vanishing.
items.strategy: Generalize the written curve Dolbeault resolution pattern directly in all dimensions ≤3 using local polydisc exactness and smooth-module acyclicity. In the standard projective cover identify finite intersections with products of C and C*, prove scalar acyclicity using explicit pseudoconvex exhaustions and scalar Dolbeault solvability (or direct Laurent solution). Expand holomorphic functions on polyannuli, prove parameter holomorphy, normal convergence and uniqueness by iterated Cauchy integrals. Decompose homogeneous degree-zero Laurent modes and give a sign-correct Čech contracting homotopy for positive degree, verifying subseries extend to the claimed charts and converge locally uniformly. Global degree-zero functions are constants. This source-guided Laurent reconstruction is not supplied by the algebraic O(m) theorem and not proved by Serre’s footnote. For the standard projective cover, intersections are C^a times (C*)^b, not polydiscs. Prove their required scalar acyclicity by an explicit annular-product Dolbeault/exhaustion or Laurent argument before using Leray; local coherent acyclicity alone does not imply it.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC; record resolutions, countable shrinking/diagonal choices, Baire/Fréchet arguments and supplier-inherited choice uses precisely. No physical premise.
